title: Chase order-independence on the full-TGD subset of ChaseBench correctness/tgds: dependency-at-a-time versus parallel chase
explanation: The program is the full-TGD subset of ChaseBench's tgds correctness scenario, a small chain of six dependencies (renamed S/TA/TB/TC/WA/WB) relating source and target relations in a data-exchange setting; side 1 hand-encodes the dependency-at-a-time chase (each dependency chased to its own fixpoint in file order, the sweep over all dependencies repeated until nothing new is derived), while side 2 is the naive-compiler translation applying all dependencies in parallel each round. The triple states the two chase orders converge to the same universal solution, illustrating the chase's order-independence for full (non-existential) dependencies.
preInWords: True; no precondition constrains the inputs.
postInWords: Each target relation computed by the dependency-at-a-time chase (TAQ, TBQ, WAQ, WBQ) equals the corresponding relation computed by the parallel chase (TA, TB, WA, WB).
family: two evaluation orders of one chase
obstructionExpectation: rate mismatch (parallel round versus one dependency per flattened iteration; nested loops flattened under five flags beside the compiled loop)
notes: The reference invariant and emitter-generated certificate were promoted from the certified Base + tools experimental answer for the unchanged input; CertificateProvenance.json records their origin and hashes.
Core.json is the canonical emitted invariant with 26 rows, including six level-1 prophecy clauses. Experimental certification outcomes and timings remain a separate result set.
sides: hand-written: s-t TGDs once, then target TGDs in file order each to its fixpoint (inner loops), sweep repeated (outer loop)
naive compiler: the six full TGDs as a Datalog program (parallel chase)
sourceProgram: ChaseBench scenarios/correctness/tgds (full TGDs; the existential t2 -> t3 dropped, t3 an input)
